concept: Socio - Religious Reform Movements in the 19th and 20th CE India
question: Which of the following social reform organisations was established in Madras in 1864?
solution:
The correct answer is __**The Veda Samaj**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Veda Samaj was established in Madras (now Chennai) in 1864.
 
• It was founded by Keshab Chandra Sen and later renamed as the Brahmo Samaj of South India.
 
• The organization aimed at promoting social reforms such as the abolition of caste distinctions and child marriage.
 
• The Veda Samaj was inspired by the principles of the Brahmo Samaj, advocating monotheism and rationalism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Brahmo Samaj:**

 
 
• Founded in 1828 by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in Calcutta (now Kolkata).
 
• It played a key role in the social and religious reform movements in India.
 
• Advocated for the abolition of practices like Sati and child marriage.
 
 
 
• **Arya Samaj:**
 
 
• Founded by Swami Dayananda Saraswati in 1875 in Bombay (now Mumbai).
 
• Promoted Vedic teachings and opposed idolatry and caste-based discrimination.
 
• Focused on education and social reform.
 
 
 
• **Prarthana Samaj:**
 
 
• Founded in 1867 in Bombay (now Mumbai) by Dr. Atmaram Pandurang.
 
• Focused on social reforms like widow remarriage and improving the status of women.
 
 
 
• **Social Reforms in 19th Century India:**
 
 
• 19th century India witnessed a wave of social reform movements aimed at eradicating social evils and promoting modernization.
 
• Leaders like Raja Ram Mohan Roy, Swami Dayananda Saraswati, and others played pivotal roles.
 
• These movements laid the foundation for subsequent reforms and the struggle for India's independence.
